- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) and model forecasts are flat or slowly rising, expect overshoot or overconfidence; adjust downward by 2–5% in early horizon.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior day), model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 3–5 days.
- If official event net supply is negative and bullish sentiment is high, model underestimates upside; add 3–7% to forecast mean for first 5 days.
- If sentiment is bearish (≤0.33) and model forecasts are rising, expect mean reversion; cap upward slope at 0.5–1.0% per day.
- When multiple auctions occur in 3–5 days, model often underestimates supply shock; add 1–3% to forecast decline for each auction.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to lag; shift forecast 1–2 days ahead for short-term (1–7 day) horizon.
- For long-term (10+ day) forecasts, model often fails to capture policy-driven mean reversion; apply 1–3% downward bias if bullish sentiment >0.7 and supply net negative.
